title: 生涯学習特別科目(NGO論)
subtitle: Special Subject - Lifelong Learning(Theory of NGO)
courseType:
(Provided by all courses)
Liberal Arts Courses
Transdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: In this course, studnets will learn about history, social backgound of NGO, wide knowledge on society and politics, solving social problems, engaging and willing to support others, utilizing those knowledges, skill and attitudes in their daily life (in future). Upon completing this course, students will be able to think by themselves how to contribute to civil society.
advice: (Outline of the course) Students will gain knowledge about NGO as well as other related actors such as civil society and volunteers in Japan and outside of Japan, public sector and private sectors' role in social activities. Students are expected to become knowledgeable and to be able to take actions by themselves after graduated. Students will learn about various actions in civil society (NGO), public sector, private sector. By the end of the course, students will learn K (Kindness of Heart), I (Intellectual Curiosity), T (Team Sprits), So that they can acquire skills and knowledges that they can practice in future. (Advice and comments) 1)Students will learn to open up their eyes to watch the world, to take interests in social issues, and keep their minds on such issues. 2)The international and social issues which will be discussed in these classes will be the issues that students may have to tackle in future. 3)The program of the course may change dependingon the number of students and circumstances of classes. 4)A lecturer of one class will be a person from NGOs, so there may be some changes in the program. 5)The lecturer of this course used to work for JBIC and JICA, as well as served as a JOCV, and as a director of an NGO.
books: 1) JANIC, 2022, NGO Databook, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (in Japanese):https://www.janic.org/blog/2022/04/22/ngodatabook2022/ 2) Worldwatch, various year, State of the World, Island press, 3) Edwards, M. and Hulme, D., 1997, Making a difference, Earthscan 4) Hulme, D, and Edwards, M. 1997, NGOs, States and Donors, Save the Children
requiredKnowledge: No specific requirements to take this course. It is desirable that students have interests in daily international issues. Some English materials will be used.

activityGoals.body: Understand and explain the expected role of NGO in society.
Argue and discuss the roles and needs of NGO in Japan.
Argue and discuss the roles of NGO in international society.
Comprehend the roles of public sectors, private sector, and civil society (NGO) in international cooperation.
Explain and plan his/her own role in future how to support NGOs.
Acquire some senses of advocacy as one of the most important role in NGO.

achievementLevels.ideal: Acquire and practice the knowledges and ideologies about NGO. As a result, after collect and select correct information, and take right actions as a global citizen base on his/her own idea/decision.
achievementLevels.standard: Learn about new knowledge and ideas related to NGOs. Think more wisely and deeply than before about social, political, economic issues than ordinary people.

lessons.content: Introduction of lecturer Guidance of the course Requests from students. What is NGO?(Public sector, private sector, civil society)
Basic data on NGO (outline, current situation, size etc) Learning about NGO by data and basic materials.
Various Types of NGOs: International NGO, Domestic NGO, NGO and NPO, Learning about different types of NGOs
Japanese NGOs: Branches of International NGOs Japanese International NGOs Others
Variety of NGOs in Japan: Pro bono, Social investment, Peer-volunteer, Self-responsibility, etc
International volunteerism through the case of the lecturer (Dobashi) (JOCV, IDEAS, IDPM, JBIC, JICA, JANNE, CAPEDS) (Some parts will overlap with "Theory of International Cooperation")
Workshop; Planning an international NGO's project As a group, plan a mock-project with given condition.
International Cooperation, ODA, Japanese ODA To learn what international cooperation and ODA means. (Some parts will overlap with "Theory of International Cooperation")
Advocacy: Pro-savanna (AJF), Human Trafficking (NFSJ), etc. Learning about advocacy, which is one of the most important role of NGOs.
NGO and money Learning how NGO collect and use money. A workshop will be held to think some original ways to collect money.
Volunteerism in Japan (the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake, other small volunteers in town, etc) Re-considering NGO through thinking about volunteerism in Japan.
International Volunteers System in the world. Learning the similarities and differences of volunteer systems in other countries.
Private sectors' Cooperate Social Responsibility IBM's volunteers, Light project of Panasonic, and others. A workshop will be held to think about things that private sectors should do.
History of Disabled People' Organization (DPO) Learning about DPOs' activities to learn different types of NGOs.
Review the whole course (wrapping-up, reviewing the scores, and conducting self-inspections). Reconsider what students can learn in this course.
